 Appearance:
Shri Pradip Kumar Gupta - Advocate for the appellant.

Shri Manish Jain - Advocate for respondents No.1 and 2
 Order

This Miscellaneous Appeal has been preferred under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the impugned award dated 24/03/2012 passed by II Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ratlam (M.P.) in Claim Case No.71/2011, whereby an amount of Rs.3,75,000/- has been awarded from the date of filing of claim petition i.e. 10/01/2011 to the respondents / claimants /
survivors of the deceased Dhanna Bai @ Dhanni Bai with interest @ 8% per annum, who died in a road traffic accident occurred on 30/10/2010.

entities.text: II Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ratlam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the appellant / Insurance Company submits that the deceased was travelling in a goods vehicle, which is against the conditions of the Insurance Policy.
Insurance Company does not cover the risk of passenger travelling in a goods vehicle, therefore, Insurance Company is not liable as liability was not covered by the Insurance policy.

He has also NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:8393 2 MA-1147-2012 opposed the cross-objection filed by the survivors of the deceased with regard to enhancement of the compensation amount.
On these grounds, learned counsel prays for allowing the appeal by dismissing the cross- objection.

3 . Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents / survivors of the deceased has opposed the appeal on the ground that though the deceased was travelling in a goods vehicle, but she was travelling in that vehicle with her goods to sell it and objection in this regard can not be raised.

For this he has invited attention of this Court towards the statement of Branch Manager Charls Joseph (DW-1).
3.1

Learned counsel in support of his cross-objection submits that learned Claims Tribunal has awarded meager amount of compensation, which is not just and proper as income of the deceased National Insurance Co. per month.

Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and Others reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 , each of the survivor is entitled for consortium amount @ Rs.40,000/-.

sentences.text:
3.3 Leaned counsel further submits that in as para 59.8 of Pranay Sethi NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:8393 3 MA-1147-2012 (Supra), the amount awarded in the heads of Funeral Expenses and Loss of Estate is to be enhanced from Rs.5,000/- each to Rs.15,000/- each.
On these contentions, learned counsel prays for allowing the cross-objection by dismissing appeal of the Insurance Company.

4. Heard and considered the rival submissions raised at bar by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5.

Branch Manager Charls Joseph (DW-1) stated in his statement before the Claims Tribunal that Insurance Policy is a package policy which covers the risk of the passengers, who were travelling along with their goods and are covered under the Insurance Policy.

The same has been discussed in para 19 to 23 by the Claims Tribunal, therefore, this Court is of the considered view that there is no perversity in the impugned award and liability to pay compensation has rightly been fastened upon the Insurance Company, hence, Insurance Company is liable for payment of compensation.

6. It is no longer res integra that where income has not been established by adducing cogent evidence, in the light of the judgment delivered by the apex Court in the case of Chandra @ Chanda @ Chandraram & Anr. Vs. Mukesh Kumar Yadav reported in (2022) 1 SCC 198 : 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3093, income of the deceased is to be assessed on the basis of circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act, therefore, on the basis of circular income of the deceased considering her as unskilled labour comes to Rs.4,145/- per month.

entities.text: Chandra @ Chanda @ Chandraram & Anr. Vs. Mukesh Kumar Yadav reported in (2022) 1 SCC 198 : 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3093
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
7. Deceased was 38 years of age at the time of accident, therefore, as per para 59.4 of Pranay Sethi (Supra) , 40% amount is added in the head of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8393 4 MA-1147-2012 Future Prospects.
8.

In the light of para 59.8 of the case Pranay Sethi (Supra) , each of claimants are entitled for consortium amount at the rate of Rs.40,000/- and in the heads of Loss of Estate and Funeral Expenses an amount of Rs.15,000/- each is to be awarded.

9. Accordingly, the just and proper compensation amount comes as under:

2 Rs.4,145/- pm + 40% FP X 12 Months Loss of Dependency: - 1/3rd Personal Expenses X Multiplier of 15 = Rs.6,96,360/-
Loss of Consortium: Rs.80,000/-
 Loss of Estate: Rs.15,000/-
 Funeral Expenses: Rs.15,000/-
 Total: Rs.8,06,360/-
 MACT Awarded: Rs.3,75,000/-
 Enhanced Amount: Rs.4,31,360/-
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.8,06,360/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.3,75,000/-.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the claimants / survivors of the deceased are entitled to enhanced amount of Rs.4,31,360/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.

10. Since the cross-objection has been valued at Rs.1,00,000/- only, therefore, the claimants are directed to pay additional court fees on the rest of the amount of Rs.3,31,360/- within a period of 30 days from today at the prevailing slab of court fees, thereafter, the same will be disbursed to the claimants.
Other terms and conditions of the impugned award including rate of interest @ 8% shall remain intact.

11. Subject to payment of requisite additional court fees within the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:8393 5 MA-1147-2012 aforesaid period, the enhanced amount shall also carry interest at the same rate.

It is made clear, in case the court fees is not paid within the stipulated period, the claimants will not be entitled for claiming interest on the enhanced amount beyond 30 days' period, till the payment of requisite court fees.
12. Resultantly, the appeal filed by the Insurance Company stands dismissed and the cross-objection filed by the claimants / survivors of the deceased sustained.
